hypothesis: If the lion's neck is one bone rather than vertebrae, every admissible public record of a normal Panthera leo neck reports exactly one cervical element and none reports two or more separate cervical bones.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (claim supported). At least one admissible source reports a cervical count for a normal lion, every reporting source reports exactly 1, and no source reports a count of 2 or more for a specimen that the source does not label as pathological.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered (claim refuted). At least one admissible source reports a cervical count of 2 or more for Panthera leo and does not describe that specimen as a pathological fusion. If some reporting sources say 1 and others say 2 or more for non-pathological animals, the verdict is mixed. If no source yields a count, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. A count taken only from a specimen the source calls pathological, with no species-typical count, is inconclusive with reason other.

test_contract.expected_observation: Public specimen manifests and published osteological descriptions of Panthera leo record a single neck bone and do not list separate cervical vertebrae.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A normal lion skeleton or a species-level vertebral formula that names two or more distinct cervical elements (atlas, axis, or cervicals numbered above 1).
test_contract.admissible_datasets: Openly fetchable specimen file lists or published anatomical descriptions that state a cervical count, or that archive separately named cervical bones, for Panthera leo. The text must identify the lion (species or a specimen of that species). Aristotle's own sentence is not a source. A comparative landmark table counts only when a row or file is identified as Panthera leo; if the lion is absent, that table is dropped and does not vote. A source that never states a cervical count is silent, not a vote for either side.
test_contract.inference_method: Count distinct cervical identities per source: an explicit integer in a vertebral formula, or the number of separately named cervical bones in a file manifest (atlas, axis, cervical I–VII, C1–C7). Support only if every voting source has count 1. Refute if any non-pathological source has count >= 2. Mixed if the voting sources disagree. No average and no modern allometric model.

interpretation: The claim is read as a species-level statement about Panthera leo: the neck is one bone, not a series of vertebrae. One normal skeleton with separate cervical bones is enough to refute that universal. The test does not ask whether the count is seven, only whether it is one. 'Pathological' is taken from the source's own wording. Fusion described as the normal lion neck would support the claim; fusion described as abnormal would not.
caveats: A web search used to locate a public lion-skeleton record returned an abstract that already stated a cervical formula, before this file was committed. The decision rule was fixed from the claim wording (one bone versus more than one) and was not changed after that abstract was seen. The counts in measured were parsed from the files by analysis.py.

The Dataverse count is the number of separately named bone directories (atlas, axis, cervical III–VII), not a measurement made by opening the meshes. Fragments of a single bone would not be labeled with those seven anatomical names.

Onwuama et al. state one formula, C7 T13 L7 S3 C20-21, for two lions. The specimen total n=3 counts those two animals plus the Dataverse skeleton. Three skeletons refute a universal claim that the neck is one bone; they are not a range-wide survey.
The journal page does not state a licence. The formula used is the public abstract on that page. The PDF was not used.
Animal Diversity Web was silent, and the Dryad landmark file returned HTTP 401, so neither voted.

deviations.what: The Dryad atlas CSV returned HTTP 401, so the landmark tables were not read and cast no vote.
deviations.why: The pre-registered contract already drops that dataset when the lion cannot be identified in it. An unreadable file cannot identify the lion. Pass and fail criteria were not changed.

deviations.what: The Animal Diversity Web account for Panthera leo states no cervical count, so it cast no vote.
deviations.why: The contract says a source that never states a count is silent. Criteria were not changed.

method: Fetched the Dataverse dataset record for Panthera leo 93 and counted distinct cervical directory names (atlas, axis, cervical III–VII). Fetched the public landing page of Onwuama et al. 2021 and read the vertebral formula in the abstract. Checked the Animal Diversity Web lion account for a cervical count and found none. Attempted the Dryad carnivoran landmark file and received HTTP 401. Applied the pre-registered rule to the sources that reported a count.
results_summary: Voting sources: 2; cervical counts: [7, 7]; specimens accounted for: 3.
Smallest reported cervical count is 7. The claim requires exactly 1.
